question: Physical buttons are increasingly disappearing from new cars and being replaced by touchscreens. The European New Car Assessment Programme (Euro NCAP) has drawn attention to the negative impact of this development, arguing that central touchscreens force drivers to take their eyes off the road and increase the risk of accidents.

The organisation has therefore announced that from 2026 onwards its five-star rating will only be given to cars that retain physical control of the five key vehicle functions: direction indicators, hazard lights, windscreen wipers, horn and SOS functions1.

The five-star safety rating is a strong asset that can mobilise car manufacturers to return to traditional buttons and knobs, but Euro NCAP, as an independent crash test organisation, cannot impose such an obligation. Does the Commission intend to introduce rules obliging car manufacturers to return to physical controls for key functions in new vehicles?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.5.2024) With a view to fostering development of new technologies, the provisions of the EU vehicle type approval legislation1 are technology- and design-neutral. The legislation does not prescribe the use of either buttons, knobs, or touchscreens as long as the safety-performance requirements are met.

Moreover, Regulation (EU) 2019/21442 lays down technical requirements to ensure a high level of general safety of vehicles and a high level of protection of vehicle occupants and vulnerable road users.

This regulation mandates new passenger cars and vans to be equipped with advanced driver assistance systems such as the driver drowsiness and attention warning system and the advanced driver distraction warning system. These systems assess the driver’s alertness and help the driver to continue to pay attention to the traffic situation by providing warning in case of any visual distraction.
Based on the above, the Commission is not considering a legislative proposal that would require the use of buttons or knobs for certain vehicle functions.
1 Regulation (EU) 2018/858 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 May 2018 on the approval and

market surveillance of motor vehicles and their trailers, and of systems, components and separate technical units intended for such vehicles, OJ L 151, 14.6.2018, p.1 –218. 2 OJ L 325, 16.12.2019, p.1-40.
